How it works

A single pool, priced like a fund.

Everyone's capital sits in one pool. The pool has a share price. Your balance is simply your shares × the current price — so performance is shared exactly in proportion to what you put in, and nobody's withdrawal changes anyone else's return.

01You deposit USDC

Send USDC on Solana to the pool wallet with your reference memo. When the transfer confirms, shares are minted to you at the price at that moment — no entry fee, no spread.

02The engine trades the pool

A signal model takes up to five concurrent positions in liquid Solana assets, sized as a fixed share of NAV. Every entry has a stop and a take-profit set at open. No discretionary overrides.

03The share price moves

NAV is marked continuously; the share price is NAV ÷ shares outstanding. It is the only number that determines your balance, and it is the same number for every holder.

04You withdraw on demand

Redeem any number of shares at the live price, paid to your own wallet from the pool's liquid USDC. If the buffer is short, the engine closes the smallest position first — never your neighbour's.

Risk disclosure
Risk disclosure

You can lose money here.

Read this before you deposit. It is short on purpose.

Past performance is not a forecast.
The +38.42% since launch describes what already happened to one pool over one period. It says nothing about the next period.
Drawdowns are normal and will happen again.
The pool has been 8.7% below its high-water mark. A future drawdown can be deeper than any shown.
The circuit breaker limits, but does not prevent, loss.
Halting on a 10% drawdown does not guarantee the loss stops at 10%. Gaps, illiquidity and failed fills can take it further.
Smart-contract and infrastructure risk.
Funds move through on-chain venues and a custody wallet. A bug, exploit or key compromise could cause total loss.
Only deposit what you can afford to lose.
This is not a savings product, is not insured, and is not investment advice.
